_comment: Infrastructure built by work-bands (DESIGN §3.2b rule 7, §3.4; DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-07, numbers DRAFT, ×3 scale). `items`: what a band can build on a hex — months for a band of `work.refPeople` people (a bigger band is proportionally faster up to `work.maxRate`, a smaller one slower), materials paid when work on that hex begins (from the cluster whose influence covers it, else from the realm stockpile; the project waits if neither has them). A paved road goes over a dirt road; a bridge goes on a river hex, is built from the bank beside it, and carries a dirt road. Movement (rule 5): a unit stepping from one road hex to another pays the terrain's cost times the road's factor, never less than `movement.minCost` for the link's level (DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-08: dirt road minimum 0.5, paved road minimum 0.25 — so on plains a dirt road doubles a unit's speed). A settlement hex counts as a dirt road for this. Mountains are one hex a month unless a road links them, then they cost 4 × the factor. `planning.bridgePenalty`: extra route cost the planner adds for a bridge still to be built, so 'road from X to Y' prefers existing bridges, settlements and short crossings; `planning.reuse`: the cost of stepping onto a hex that already has the road.

items.name: Dirt road
items.blurb: Cleared and levelled; halves the cost of rough ground between two road hexes.

items.name: Paved road
items.blurb: Stone-laid over a dirt road; cheaper still to travel and the road food and trade will use later.

items.name: Bridge
items.blurb: Joins both banks of a river hex and carries a dirt road across.
